newsitem.title: FRANCE: Kohl, Chirac start Franco-German summit on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Chirac start Franco-German summit on EMU.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl arrived in Poitiers on Friday for a summit with conservative President Jacques Chirac and France's new Socialist government on a controversial European Union budget pact.

Chirac greeted Kohl with military honours at a high-tech theme park outside the western French city. Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, who is demanding new EU commitments on growth and jobs as a condition for accepting a pact limiting the deficits of countries that join a single European currency, was to arrive later for separate talks with Kohl.

French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn was holding separate talks with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel. French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine was also meeting his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel.
Chirac, Kohl and Jospin were to hold a joint news conference after the summit at 4 p.m. (1400 GMT).
The meeting is a first international test of "cohabitation" power-sharing between conservative Chirac and Jospin since the left swept to power in France after last week's parliamentary election.

Chirac has said he believes European Union leaders will be able to satisfy the French demands and sign a pact, limiting deficits after the launch of the euro single currency, at a summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17.
